partial_case.facts: The resident lives in a 2-bedroom semi-detached house. The landlord is aware the resident has mental health vulnerabilities and does not have digital access. She said she was unhappy with the landlord's response to her reports of anti-social behaviour (ASB). She was also unhappy they had not provided a copy of the homes Energy Performance Certificate (EPC). In April-May 2022, the resident told the landlord children were kicking balls over her fence, and she felt intimidated. She said she was unhappy with the quality of the fencing previously installed. The landlord raised an order to fit an Air Sourced Heat Pump. This involved updating the home's Energy Performance Certificate. In June-July 2022, the resident reported children kicking balls into her garden and requested security lighting and CCTV to be installed. The landlord's contractor then reported the resident was distressed and had spoken about ongoing issues with neighbours. The landlord called the resident to discuss. The landlord inspected the fence and said there were no issues with it. It said it would not carry out further work on the fence. In January 2023, the landlord and the resident's MP communicated about the Energy Performance Certificate, a neighbour dispute and ongoing repairs. On 2 March 2023, in her stage 1 complaint the resident said she felt the landlord was hiding something as it had not provided a copy of the Energy Performance Certificate. She reported receiving 'hell' from her neighbours and gaps in the fencing were part of this. She wanted compensation and a manager to visit her. She felt the landlord was discriminating against her. In March 2023, the landlord spoke directly to the resident and held an internal case conference to discuss options for support. The resident told the landlord she did not want a visit, and she did not want it to speak to her neighbours directly. On 22 March 2023, the landlord gave a stage 1 response. It provided a copy of the Energy Performance Certificate. It said it would install an external light sensor, and the resident could buy CCTV if she wished. It said it had offered to contact the neighbours, but the resident had declined this offer. It would inspect the fence for gaps. It said the offer of a manager visit remained open. It asked for specific examples of how the resident felt discriminated against, so it could investigate. On 3 April 2023, the resident told the landlord she had received 2 letters about the Energy Performance Certificate, and she felt this was harassment. Between 27 April - 10 May 2023, the MP told the landlord the resident was very anxious about children kicking footballs and entering the garden to retrieve them. The landlord called the resident twice but was unable to leave a message. On 10 May 2023, the resident cancelled the external light sensor job. On 26 June 2023, the resident escalated her complaint. She repeated the same issues raised at stage 1. On 27 July 2023, the landlord gave a stage 2 response. The response maintained the position set out in the stage 1 response about the Energy Performance Certificate, ASB and discrimination. It agreed to do some fencing repairs and said it would call the resident in September and October to ensure all works were completed. The resident asked this Service to investigate as she was unhappy about the landlord's handling of her Energy Performance Certificate request and her reports of ASB. She said she found the situation very distressing, and it was impacting her health. In October 2025 she said the neighbours had left. However, she wanted the landlord to recognise the impact of the events.

It did not fully respond to her requests for security lights and fencing repairs in 2022. When it committed to fencing repairs, it did not evidence these were completed. It did not acknowledge these failings in its complaint response.
The landlord responded appropriately to the resident's request and considered her vulnerabilities when it provided a copy of the Energy Performance Certificate.
The landlord responded appropriately to the resident's complaint of discrimination and offered to investigate specific examples if these were provided.
The landlord did not acknowledge the initial complaint and was delayed in responding to its stage 1 and 2 complaints.

partial_case.facts: The resident lives in a 2-bedroom semi-detached house, and the landlord was aware she had mental health vulnerabilities and no digital access. She was unhappy with the landlord’s response to reports of anti-social behaviour and with not being provided a copy of the home’s Energy Performance Certificate. The complaint concerned reports of ASB and associated fencing repairs, a request for an Energy Performance Certificate, discrimination, and complaint handling. From April to May 2022, the resident told the landlord that children were kicking balls over her fence, that she felt intimidated, and that she was unhappy with the quality of previously installed fencing. In June to July 2022, the resident reported children kicking balls into her garden and requested security lighting and CCTV; the landlord later inspected the fence and said it would not carry out further work. On 2 March 2023, the resident made a stage 1 complaint about the Energy Performance Certificate, neighbour issues, fencing gaps, compensation, a manager visit, and discrimination. On 22 March 2023, the landlord gave a stage 1 response providing the Energy Performance Certificate and addressing lighting, CCTV, neighbour contact, fence inspection, manager visit, and discrimination examples. On 26 June 2023, the resident escalated her complaint, and on 27 July 2023 the landlord gave a stage 2 response maintaining its position on the Energy Performance Certificate, ASB and discrimination, while agreeing to some fencing repairs and follow-up calls. The resident referred the matter to the Ombudsman because she was unhappy about the landlord’s handling of her Energy Performance Certificate request and ASB reports, and she said the situation was distressing and affecting her health.
